newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones union submits proxy for meeting.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones union submits proxy for meeting.

text.p: A proxy proposal has been submitted to Dow Jones & Co Inc for next Wednesday's annual shareholders' meeting which seeks to link the pay of company chief executive Peter Kann closely to company performance.

The Independent Association of Publishers' Employees, a union representing 2,400 Dow Jones staff, said it submitted a proxy which urges the firm to set a formula for Kann's pay and to have it administered by independent directors.
"Kann received a 74 percent increase in compensation from 1992 through 1995 even as Dow Jones became the worst performer in the S&P 500 publishing index," the union said.
It said its calculations did not include stock grants or awards of restricted stock to Kann.
Dow Jones spokesman Roger May said it was possible to support any case by carefully choosing comparison periods, and he noted the board opposed a move to a fixed pay formula.
"The board opposes the proposals made by IAPE," May said, citing current compensation committee practices which he said allows for flexibility.
He said the IAPE's proxy was the only one not submitted by the board for the meeting.

Dow Jones's shareholder meeting is expected to be unusually stormy because several big shareholders oppose the company's plan to spend $650 million over four years on revamping Dow Jones Markets, its financial information services unit. ((-- New York Newsrom 212 859 1610))
